# HeyMate

> HeyMate is a free, open-source (MIT) AI assistant for macOS that lives in the MacBook notch. Hold Control + Option, ask about anything on your screen, and it answers out loud while its cursor points at what it means. It can also hand real coding work to Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode, and it runs on the CLI subscriptions you already have: no HeyMate account and no second API bill.

- Website: https://getheymate.vercel.app
- Source code: https://github.com/UmarSiddiqui/heymate
- Download (latest macOS build): https://github.com/UmarSiddiqui/heymate/releases/latest/download/HeyMate.dmg
- Release notes: https://github.com/UmarSiddiqui/heymate/releases
- 38-second demo video: https://getheymate.vercel.app/assets/video/heymate-demo-v2.mp4
- Privacy notes: https://getheymate.vercel.app/privacy
- Changelog: https://getheymate.vercel.app/changelog
- Permissions explained: https://getheymate.vercel.app/permissions
- Guide for developers, designers, and learners: https://getheymate.vercel.app/how-to-use-heymate

## Key facts

- Platform: macOS 14.2 or later, Apple silicon and Intel. Works on Macs without a notch (a top-center pill instead).
- Price: free. MIT licensed. Built in native SwiftUI.
- AI "brains": the user's existing ChatGPT plan (through the Codex CLI) or Claude plan (through the Claude Code CLI). Onboarding asks "Which AI do you already pay for?", installs the official CLI if missing, and signs in through the browser with one click. "Neither" uses Apple Intelligence on-device. OpenCode and a custom Anthropic-compatible API are also supported.
- Push-to-talk: hold Control + Option, speak, release. Voice input uses on-device Apple Speech and the macOS system voice by default.
- Screen awareness: HeyMate captures the screen only when a question needs it. Screenshots are never stored or added to chat history. Password managers and System Settings are excluded from capture.
- Data: chats, memory, mates, and routines are stored locally in ~/Library/Application Support/heymate/. Credentials live in the macOS Keychain. There is no HeyMate server.
- Builds are signed with a stable self-signed certificate, not Apple Developer ID, and are not notarized. The Terminal install (`curl -fsSL https://getheymate.vercel.app/install.sh | bash`) or Homebrew (`brew install umarsiddiqui/tap/heymate`) avoids the macOS warning. HeyMate updates itself.

## Features

- Notch home: hover the notch to open Home, Apps, and Agents. No dock icon, no menu-bar clutter.
- Notch micro-apps: File Shelf with AirDrop, focus timers, Clipboard history, Now Playing with album art, Downloads, Camera Mirror, Volume and Brightness/keyboard-backlight HUDs, Bluetooth devices, Battery, Next Event, Reminders.
- Coding agents with an approval gate: the agent first writes a read-only plan in a sandbox folder (~/Projects/heymate). Nothing is written until the user approves. Approved work runs in a background helper that survives quitting the app, with undo snapshots and Terminal takeover.
- Standing Orders: HeyMate proposes work but never starts it unasked.
- Mates: persistent helpers with a name, job, personality, face, memory, and workspace folder. Routines run a mate daily at a set time or every N hours.
- Connectors: Apple Calendar, Reminders, Notes, Mail, Messages, and Shortcuts; local CLIs such as gh, git, docker, kubectl, vercel, supabase, and stripe; any MCP server; 1,400+ toolkits via Composio (with the user's own free Composio key). Read-only calls run quietly; anything that sends, deletes, or pays asks first.

## How HeyMate compares

- Unlike chat apps in a browser tab, HeyMate sees the current screen on request and points at the answer on screen.
- Unlike hosted agent products, coding agents run through the user's own Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode CLI and cannot write files before the user approves a plan.
- Unlike menu-bar utilities, it uses the otherwise unused space around the MacBook camera notch.

## HeyMate vs Boring Notch

HeyMate is an alternative to Boring Notch (a popular open-source notch utility) that adds an AI assistant. Both offer Now Playing controls with album art and a visualizer, calendar, a file shelf with AirDrop, battery and charging status, volume, brightness, and keyboard-backlight HUDs, Bluetooth connect/disconnect activity, a camera mirror, and hover-to-open. HeyMate adds focus timers, clipboard history, downloads, and reminders in the notch, plus push-to-talk screen-aware answers, a pointing cursor, approval-gated Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode agents, and mates with scheduled routines. Boring Notch is GPL-3.0; HeyMate is MIT.

## Install

1. In Terminal: `curl -fsSL https://getheymate.vercel.app/install.sh | bash`, or `brew install umarsiddiqui/tap/heymate`. (Or download HeyMate.dmg from the latest GitHub release; if macOS can't verify it, open System Settings > Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.)
2. Grant Microphone, Accessibility, and Screen Recording.
3. Pick the AI you already pay for (Claude or ChatGPT) and click sign in. Choose Neither to use Apple Intelligence on-device.
4. Hold Control + Option and say hey.
